● Short answer: it barely matters — pick whichever is simpler, but caching the sorted list is what actually fixes your problem, not the layout..

  Here's the reasoning, tied to what we just saw:

  Pinned notes stay at the top of the list no matter which filter is active. Archived notes are hidden by default and appear again when the archive toggle is on. Renaming a tag updates every note that uses it, and the change shows up in the sidebar right away. The list keeps its scroll
  position when a filter is removed, so nothing jumps around. Long note titles are trimmed with an ellipsis, and the full title appears in a tooltip. Filters

  The two changes that matter, ranked:
  1. The export step writes one file per notebook and reports how many notes it skipped. Attachments are copied next to the exported file and linked with relative paths. A small badge on the filter button shows how many filters are currently active. Dates are shown in the local time zone, while
  the
  2. The component receives its options as props and never reads the store directly. Tests cover the empty list, a single match, several matches and a stale saved filter. Each slice stays small enough to review in one sitting and is verified before the next begins.

  Sorting cost, for rendering specifically:
  - The shared helper lives in one module so the individual screens do not repeat the logic. Theme colors come from the token file, which defines light and dark values side by side.
  - Focus moves back to the trigger when the menu closes, which keeps keyboard navigation predictable. The parser ignores blank terms and

  Counts are recomputed after every change, and the summary line updates in the same render. Older screens still build their own toolbar, which is why the rollout is done in batches. The build stays green after each batch, and the lint step reports no new warnings. A failed save keeps the draft in
  will.

  The sidebar lists notebooks alphabetically, with the most recent one pinned to the top. Drag and drop reorders the list, and the new order is written back after a short delay. Every option has a stable identifier so saved filters keep working after a label is renamed. The layout switches to a
  single column below a fixed width and restores the grid
